verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own SDK docs show non-boolean flag values: `useFeatureValue("button-color", "blue")` returns a string, `getFeatureValue` sits alongside `isOn`, and rules and targeting control which values a user sees. Experiment rules assign users into multiple variations, which covers the multivariate part of the story. Number and JSON value types are never shown, and the hands-on probe only exercised a boolean flag. missing for 10: explicit documentation of number and JSON value types, hands-on evidence of a non-boolean or JSON config value being served.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve multivariate flags and dynamic configuration values (strings, numbers, JSON), not just booleans

citations.quote: There are 2 main methods for evaluating features: `isOn` and `getFeatureValue`
Add targeting conditions to a rule to control which values a user sees.
you can add an experiment rule to a feature that will randomly assign the users based on some hashing attribute into one of your experiment variations.
